links.comparator_used: Non-AI primary care sites where patients are referred to eyecare for DED testing (difference-in-difference, 2019 vs 2021)
links.outcome: Adherence to annual diabetic eye disease testing (HEDIS measure), including among Black/African American patients and the equity gap
links.effect: Odds ratio of adherence at AI-switched sites was 36% higher than at non-AI sites; Black/African American adherence increased 11.9% at AI-switched sites vs decreased 1.2% at non-AI sites; Asian American vs Black/African American gap shrank from 15.6% (61.1% vs 45.5%) to 3.5%
links.quote: First, after controlling for a wide range of potential confounders, our regression analysis demonstrated that the odds ratio of adherence at AI-switched sites was 36% higher than that of non-AI sites, suggesting that there was a higher increase in DED testing between 2019 and 2021 at AI-switched sites than at non-AI sites.

design_hint: Point-of-care autonomous AI screening deployment in primary care vs. referral to eyecare
